definition: The emission of electrons from a metal surface when electromagnetic radiation above the metal's threshold frequency falls on it. It is evidence that light behaves as particles (photons).
The minimum frequency of electromagnetic radiation that can release photoelectrons from a given metal, $f_0 = \frac{\Phi}{h}$. Below it no electrons are emitted, however intense the radiation.
The minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the surface of a metal, written $\Phi$. It equals $hf_0$, where $f_0$ is the threshold frequency.
The kinetic energy of the fastest electrons emitted in the photoelectric effect, $E_\text{max} = hf - \Phi$. It depends on the frequency of the radiation and the metal, not on the intensity.
